newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Drugs chief warns on planned SAfrica health reform.
newsitem.headline: Drugs chief warns on planned SAfrica health reform.

text.p: South Africa faces the prospect of losing foreign investment from drugmakers and strangling new research if it takes a hard line in proposed health reforms, a senior industry figure said on Wednesday.

Sean Lance, president of the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers' Associations, said foreign companies needed a welcoming legislative environment to invest in and there was a threat South Africa was not providing it.
"The threat is very real," he said.

Draft legislation put forward by Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma last week has upset the industry which says it aims for mandatory substitution of off-patent branded drugs with cheaper generic versions and also attacks the industry's right to promote its brand names.
The draft states: "No person shall sell any medicine to the State if that medicine contains the brand name in its label."
Lance, who is also chief executive designate of the world's biggest drugs firm Glaxo Wellcome Plc, said the industry welcomed generics, but that free competition should decide if they are used.
"We should all be involved in this game together," he told reporters.
Lance blasted any possible move against brand names. "(The government) would be sending very definite signals to industry if it tampered with these inviolate symbols," he said.

Zuma's relationship with the drugs industry has been marked by conflict. When the proposals were originally put forward last year Anglo-U.S. drugs firm SmithKline Beecham Plc took the matter to court, forcing Zuma to back down and launch a consultative process.
But the industry says the new proposals differ little from the original ones.

Lance said the main threat to the local industry was not in the loss of jobs, but in the potentially devastating effect they would have on medical research in South Africa's well-respected academic community.

"If you look at countries where the treatment of the industry has not been good you can very clearly see that the research-based industry has withdrawn its interest... if you have not been rewarded for innovation in that country, why would you do it?" he said.
South Africa's Pharmaceutical Manufacturers' Association has said that the industry is thinking about renewing its legal challenge against the reforms, but that no decision has yet been made.
